statement: Dynamic lookahead (examining K = n/4 candidate pieces) is the dominant improvement mechanism for greedy skyline packing, contributing ~63% of total score improvement (6.94 of 11.10 points over the iter-1 baseline). The mechanism allows the greedy packer to escape locally suboptimal choices by selecting the best-fitting piece from a window rather than the fixed-order next piece.
regime: Random polyominoes (k=1-10, n=100-10000), 2-second time limit, greedy skyline placement
mechanism: At each step, the packer examines min(n/4, remaining) candidate pieces and selects the one whose best orientation minimizes global height. This avoids placing large pieces in suboptimal positions and matches small pieces to skyline gaps. The window is dynamically adjusted for large instances to stay within the 2s time limit.
applicability_bounds: Holds for the specific polyomino packing problem with random inputs (k=1-10). The 63% contribution figure is for the combined baseline of roughness + compaction + multi-ordering; the absolute lookahead contribution depends on what other improvements are present. May not hold for structured (non-random) inputs where piece ordering matters less.

statement: Secondary packing improvements (roughness tiebreaker, column compaction, multi-ordering with hybrid time strategy) contribute ~4 points over the iter-1 skyline baseline (~76 vs ~72), independent of lookahead. These are complementary but not individually dominant.
mechanism: Roughness tiebreaker keeps skyline smooth for future placements. Column compaction removes empty columns to reduce effective width. Multi-ordering tries 3 strategies (ascending-min-dim, descending-cell-count, descending-max-dim) to capture different packing opportunities. Hybrid time strategy allocates 60% to width sweep and 40% to alternative orderings.
applicability_bounds: The ~4 point improvement is measured against the iter-1 skyline packer (no roughness, no compaction, single ordering). The absolute contribution may vary with different baseline implementations.

statement: The skyline packer's score is sensitive to time-managed width sweep budget — system load variations can cause score ranges of 6+ points (observed: 79.88-86.16 for h-main, range 6.28) even with the hybrid time strategy. Without lookahead, variance paradoxically decreases (range 2.46) because faster pack calls allow more width exploration within the budget.
regime: Random polyominoes with time-managed packing under 2s limit
mechanism: Lookahead increases per-pack-call cost by factor ~K, reducing the number of widths that can be explored in phase 1. When system load is high, fewer widths are tried, potentially missing the optimal width. Without lookahead, each pack call is O(n) not O(n*K), so many more widths fit in the budget, reducing variance. The hybrid time strategy (60/40 phase split) mitigates but does not eliminate this effect.
applicability_bounds: Variance depends on the ratio of per-pack-call time to total time budget. In regimes with generous time budgets, this effect diminishes.
